chapter: Lester Young and the early Basie years
title: Newport 1958: rehearsing with Billie Holiday and Prez's wounded feelings
summary: At Newport, Tate plays with Goodman's band and with Billie and Prez, whose feelings are hurt when the group laughs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: And he told me that, you know, like the last time I was with him. See, I was with him -- the last time I was with him, Gary, was -- we played up in -- up here for George Wein--- Newport.

That's when they were having the festival. Well, I played there the first night with Benny Goodman's big band. That was in '58. And, of course, John had made us stay over to play for Billie and me and Pee-wee and Jack T., Georgie Auld and Prez and Buck, Jo Jones. I don't remember who -- Walter Page. That was the rhythm section. I don't remember who we had on piano. So we all stayed there and played for -- I stayed -- as a matter of fact, I did two days, you know. I stayed there and did the -- after Benny's concert, I stayed there and did the next day.

So Prez was -- he was sick then. It was getting to him, you know, he was really failing. He was short-winded, he didn't have any stamina, couldn't hardly fill his horn, you know what I mean? Sound -- couldn't control his sound. So that day, we had a rehearsal, rehearsing things with Billie. So George and I was always tight, you know? Georgie always -- I'll show you, on the other hand -- he calls me Miss Tate and
I call him Mrs. Auld. We always -- "Hello, Miss Tate," right now, you know, he'd do it.

So anyway, we were there playing. So Prez couldn't find the place. The hall was really hard to find. And Prez is sincere about everything. I mean, like he didn't even want to be late, you know. We'd been playing about an hour, rehearsing about an hour and a half, just going over some things to play for her and little riffs and things we was going to play behind Billie, you know. So man, when he came in, when he found that place, he came in and he ran -- when he walked to the door, like he'd come in from that foyer there and he stops and he spies us and he got this big wide hat on and the crown's about that high. And he really looked comical, you know? And man, everybody broke down and started laughing. Said, "You finally found us, Prez." And man, it hurt his feelings, you know, because everybody was laughing at him. He says, "I don't see what's so fucking funny with you ladies." He says, "I've been looking for this fucker for two hours and a half and there ain't a damn thing funny."

He said, "Now, I don't see nothing for you all to laugh about." So we says, "Oh, Prez, we didn't mean anything like that," you know, "we just --" You know. He told me later on, he says, "Hey, Tate, you know," -- this is when he and I

were together, "you know, I was really surprised that you laughed at me." I said, "No, we weren't laughing at you. We just --" I said, "I had a hard time finding the damn place myself." I said, "George and I, he and I came in a car." George had one of those little high-powered cars then. I don't know what the hell it was, but it was one of those -- and he and I had a hell of a time finding it. So I said, "No, we didn't mean it like that." So he was all right after that. Just give you an idea of how sensitive he was, you know.
